on_metcalfe_rock.blurb: Metcalfe Rock is a dolostone cliff in Ontario, reached from Collingwood by way of Grey Road 19 and 10 Line. It sits among trees and stays shaded for most of the day. The face is divided into eleven small crags, with Overhanging Wall, Golf Town, Malen's Wall and Metcalfe North holding the most routes. Sport lines outnumber trad, though both are well represented, and some older mixed-gear lines have been re-bolted as sport while new moderate sport routes have been added. Grades run from easy ground up to 5.13, but most routes fall between 5.8 and 5.11, with 5.10 the most common, so it suits beginners and solid intermediates as well as people looking for a steeper challenge.

bc_comox_lake_2.blurb: Comox Lake is a cluster of basalt crags on Vancouver Island, near Cumberland and roughly an hour north of Nanaimo. The crags sit a few minutes apart, so a day can take in several of them. Sport routes make up the large majority, with a smaller group of trad lines and a couple of top ropes, and there is bouldering too. The grades cluster in the 5.10 and 5.11 range, with a modest spread of easier routes below and a few 5.12s and 5.13s above. Larger sub-areas include Downtown Eastside, Main Wall, Raven Wall and Upper East Side, and Waterfall Wall is the one with mostly trad.

co_golden_gate_canyon_sp.blurb: Golden Gate Canyon State Park lies in the mountains above Golden, Colorado. The park's crags are mostly granite, at roughly 8,000 to 10,000 feet, and range from about 50 to 450 feet tall. Climbs are scattered through the backcountry rather than gathered at one roadside wall, and some approaches take over an hour. Traditional routes lead, with sport routes added more recently and a smaller set of boulder problems, such as those at Rifleman Phillips Bouldering. Grades range widely, but the middle of the spread is 5.9 to 5.11. Dude's Throne, Mt. Thorodin and The Grendel are the larger crags by route count, while Little Dude is a short crag with bolted lines from moderate to hard.

mt_billings_rimrocks.blurb: The Billings Rimrocks are sandstone cliffs that wrap around the edge of Billings, Montana, known locally as the Rims. Trad, top-rope and sport climbing are all common, and top roping is possible on nearly every route. Most grades fall between 5.8 and 5.12, with 5.9 to 5.11 the heart of it, plus some bouldering. The main zones are the cliff above the Gregory subdivision, Phipps Park and Rockwood Circle. Winter is a good season here, while summer days get hot by mid-morning and south-facing walls bake at midday. The rock can be loose, so helmets are wise.

nv_gateway_canyon_boulders.blurb: Gateway Canyon is the bouldering canyon at the north end of Red Rock, in the Calico Basin side of the range. Every climb here is a boulder problem, on sandstone that is fragile and easily damaged when wet. The trail loops around the back of Kraft Mountain from Monkey Bar Boulder, and the first boulders are about 25 minutes along, the farthest around 40. The problems are spread out rather than packed together, and the ground beyond the Kraft Boulders is cooler and shadier. Grades run from V0 through the double digits, with most between V1 and V8. South Seas Bouldering, Swirly Cliff Boulders and Outback Boulder are among the larger sub-areas. At Red Rock in general, winter is the usual time to boulder.
